message.content:
Below is a **7‑day “Paris in a Week”** itinerary that balances the classic must‑see sights with some off‑the‑beaten‑path experiences.  
Feel free to tweak the days or swap activities to match your interests (art, food, shopping, history, etc.). All times are approximate and can be adjusted on the fly.

---

## 1️⃣ Pre‑Trip Checklist

| Item | Details |
|------|---------|
| **Passport & Visa** | Passport valid at least 6 months beyond your return. EU/US/Canada/UK citizens can enter visa‑free for 90 days. |
| **Flights** | Book round‑trip from your nearest major hub to Charles de Gaulle (CDG) or Orly (ORY). Look for airlines that offer free checked bags if you’re traveling light. |
| **Currency** | Euro (€). Credit cards (Visa/MasterCard) accepted everywhere; carry a small amount of cash for metro tickets, cafés, and markets. |
| **Language Basics** | “Bonjour” (hello), “Merci” (thank you), “S’il vous plaît” (please), “Où est…?” (Where is…). A pocket phrasebook or a language app helps. |
| **Travel Insurance** | Covers health, trip cancellation, lost luggage. |
| **Packing List** | Light layers, comfortable walking shoes, power adapter (Type C/F), reusable water bottle, small daypack, copy of passport, travel guide or offline map app. |
| **Health** | Check COVID‑19 requirements (if any). Bring any prescription meds in original packaging. |

---

## 2️⃣ Day‑by‑Day Itinerary

> **Tip:** Use the Paris Metro (Line 1–14) for quick travel. Buy a *carnet* of 10 single‑ride tickets or a *Paris Visite* pass for unlimited rides.  

### Day 1 – Arrival & Montmartre

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| **Morning** | Arrive at CDG/ORY → take RER B to Gare du Nord → transfer to Metro Line 2 to **Abbesses**. |
| **Late Morning** | Check into hotel (see suggestions below). |
| **Afternoon** | Explore **Montmartre**: Sacré‑Coeur, Place du Tertre, artists’ square. |
| **Evening** | Dinner at **Le Consulat** (classic French bistro). |
| **Night** | Optional: catch a cabaret at **Moulin Rouge** or stroll along the Seine. |

### Day 2 – Classic Landmarks

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| **Morning** | Visit **Eiffel Tower** (buy tickets online to skip the line). |
| **Mid‑Morning** | Walk through **Champ de Mars** → head to **Trocadéro Gardens** for photos. |
| **Lunch** | Picnic at **Jardin du Champ de Mars** (grab baguette, cheese, wine). |
| **Afternoon** | Take Metro to **Champs‑Élysées** → Arc de Triomphe (climb to top). |
| **Evening** | Dinner at **L’Avenue** (famous for celebrity clientele). |
| **Night** | Seine river cruise (Bateaux Mouches) – sunset view. |

### Day 3 – Louvre & Palais Royal

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| **Morning** | Louvre Museum (arrive early, 9 am). Focus on the Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo, and the Egyptian wing. |
| **Lunch** | Café Marly inside Louvre or nearby **Café Richelieu**. |
| **Afternoon** | Walk to **Palais Royal** gardens → explore the boutiques. |
| **Evening** | Dinner at **Le Grand Véfour** (Michelin‑starred). |
| **Night** | Optional: attend a classical concert at the **Opéra Garnier**. |

### Day 4 – Day Trip to Versailles

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| **Morning** | Take RER C from **Saint‑Charles** to **Versailles Château** (tickets online). |
| **Mid‑Morning** | Tour the Hall of Mirrors, King’s Apartments, and the Gardens. |
| **Lunch** | Eat at **La Petite Venise** inside the palace grounds. |
| **Afternoon** | Continue exploring the Gardens, Trianon Palaces, and Marie‑Antoinette’s Estate. |
| **Evening** | Return to Paris via RER C. |
| **Night** | Light dinner near your hotel or try a local bistro like **Le Petit Cler**. |

### Day 5 – Latin Quarter & Notre‑Dame

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| **Morning** | Walk through **Latin Quarter**: Sorbonne, Panthéon, Rue Mouffetard market. |
| **Lunch** | Try **Le Coupe Chou** for classic French cuisine. |
| **Afternoon** | Visit **Notre‑Dame** (exterior only, interior still under restoration). |
| **Evening** | Explore **Île Saint-Louis** → dessert at **Berthillon** ice cream. |
| **Night** | Optional: jazz club at **Le Caveau de la Huchette**. |

### Day 6 – Musée d’Orsay & Saint‑Germain

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| **Morning** | Musée d’Orsay (Impressionist masterpieces). |
| **Lunch** | Café on the museum terrace overlooking the Seine. |
| **Afternoon** | Stroll to **Saint‑Germain‑en‑Laye** (if you’re up for a short train ride) or stay in Paris: visit **Luxembourg Gardens**. |
| **Evening** | Dinner at **Septime** (reservations required). |
| **Night** | Walk along the Seine, cross the Pont Alexandre III for night views. |

### Day 7 – Shopping & Departure

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| **Morning** | Visit **Galeries Lafayette** and **Printemps** on Boulevard Haussmann. |
| **Lunch** | Grab a sandwich at **Le Pain Quotidien** inside Galeries Lafayette. |
| **Afternoon** | Last‑minute souvenir shopping in **Le Marais** (boutiques, vintage shops). |
| **Departure** | Head to CDG/ORY via RER B or taxi. |

---

## 3️⃣ Accommodation Suggestions

| Hotel | Neighborhood | Price Range (per night) | Highlights |
|-------|--------------|------------------------|------------|
| **Hotel Le Meurice** | 1st Arrondissement | €350–€600 | Luxury, classic décor, Michelin‑starred restaurant. |
| **Hôtel Ekta** | 8th Arrondissement | €150–€250 | Chic boutique, close to Champs‑Élysées. |
| **Hotel Henriette** | Marais (4th Arrondissement) | €120–€200 | Boutique, art deco, central location. |
| **Hôtel du Petit Moulin** | Montmartre (18th Arrondissement) | €80–€140 | Budget‑friendly, bohemian vibe. |
| **Airbnb** | Various | €70–€180 | Choose a studio or one‑bedroom in a quiet neighborhood. |

> **Tip:** Book hotels with free cancellation in case plans change.  

---

## 4️⃣ Dining Highlights (Must‑Try)

| Dish | Restaurant | Why |
|------|------------|-----|
| Croissants & café au lait | **Du Pain et des Idées** | Legendary croissants. |
| Escargot | **L’Arpège** | Michelin‑starred, creative French cuisine. |
| Coq au vin | **Le Relais de l’Entrecôte** | Classic French steakhouse. |
| Macarons | **Ladurée** | Iconic Parisian sweets. |
| Cheese platter | **Fromagerie Barthélemy** | Artisan cheese selection. |
| Crêpes | **Crêperie Bretonne** | Traditional Breton crêpes. |

---

## 5️⃣ Budget Estimate (per person)

| Category | Cost (EUR) |
|----------|------------|
| Flights (round‑trip) | 300–800 |
| Accommodation (7 nights) | 700–2100 |
| Metro & RER passes | 30–50 |
| Attractions (tickets) | 100–200 |
| Meals | 300–500 |
| Miscellaneous (souvenirs, tips) | 100–200 |
| **Total** | **~1530–~4100** |

> **Tip:** Use a travel card (e.g., Revolut, N26) for better exchange rates and lower fees.  

---

## 6️⃣ Packing Essentials

| Item | Notes |
|------|-------|
| Comfortable walking shoes | Paris streets can be uneven. |
| Light jacket & umbrella | Weather can be unpredictable. |
| Power adapter (Type C/F) | 230 V, 50 Hz. |
| Reusable water bottle | Stay hydrated. |
| Small daypack | For daily essentials. |
| Copy of passport & travel documents | Keep separate from originals. |
| Basic first aid kit | Band‑ages, pain relievers, motion sickness tablets. |
| Travel guide or offline map app | Google Maps offline packs. |

---

## 7️⃣ Safety & Etiquette

| Topic | Advice |
|-------|--------|
| Pickpocketing | Keep valuables in a front pocket or money belt. |
| Tipping | 5–10 % for good service; rounding up is common. |
| Language | Politeness matters; a simple “Bonjour” goes a long way. |
| Public transport etiquette | Queue at the front, keep noise low. |
| Cultural norms | Dress modestly when visiting churches; cover shoulders. |

---

## 8️⃣ Quick Reference Map

- **Metro Map**: [Google Maps – Paris Metro](https://goo.gl/maps/ParisMetro)
- **RER Map**: [RER Lines](https://goo.gl/maps/RERParis)
- **Walking Distance Calculator**: [Walk Score – Paris](https://www.walkscore.com/Paris)

---

### Final Thought

Paris is a city that rewards curiosity. While the itinerary above covers the highlights, leave a few hours each day for spontaneous discoveries—whether it’s a hidden courtyard café, a street performer, or a pop‑up art exhibit. Enjoy your trip! Bon voyage!
